name: Peter Mandelson
role: British Labour politician: cabinet minister, EU Trade Commissioner (2004-2008), Business Secretary (2008-2010), UK ambassador to the US (2025)
summary: Architect of New Labour's modernisation, he combined acceptance of markets, private enterprise and low redistribution with an activist role for government in industry and innovation. He is a consistent pro-EU, pro-euro and pro-trade voice who opposed Brexit, backed enlargement and a reformed EU, and supported the UN route on Iraq. Many positions on social, liberty and ecology questions are not recorded.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: He called hereditary peerages the least legitimate part of the honours system (4 Mar 1993, col. 459) and attacked the hereditary Conservative majority in the Lords (2 Feb 1999, col. 763); the evidence concerns peerages, not all hereditary rank.

abolish-ip.rationale: As Business Secretary he drove copyright enforcement, including a graduated response that could end in disconnection of persistent infringers.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: In 2009 opposed cutting spending during the recession and wanted stimulus kept until recovery was secure, with debt reduced by a credible plan.

ban-cartels.rationale: As Trade and Industry Secretary he said the Government would use the Competition Act to attack anti-competitive practices (Commons, 16 Dec 1998, col. 969).

common-currency.rationale: He said a single currency is the sensible and logical extension of the single market and that British entry was a matter of when, not if (Commons, 18 June 2002, cols. 180-181).

decide-locally.rationale: He called for devolution of power 'outwards and downwards' (11 July 1994, col. 728), mechanisms against unnecessary EU centralisation (18 June 2002) and English regional assemblies (Commons, 2001-03).

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: As Northern Ireland Secretary he defended the principle of consent: the people of Northern Ireland alone decide by their vote where it belongs (Commons, 16 May 2000, col. 263).

drastic-climate-action.rationale: He called climate change a crisis requiring trade and other policy to change (Oslo, 18 Sep 2008).

empower-international-orgs.rationale: On Iraq he wanted the UN made into a 'hard instrument of collective international action' that enforces its demands (Commons, 24 Sep 2002, col. 90).

expand-nuclear.rationale: As Business Secretary he funded a nuclear manufacturing research centre and a nuclear low carbon area so British firms could win work building new nuclear power stations.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: He urged welcoming sovereign wealth fund investment and warned against suspicion turning into protectionism, saying states already hold legal means against inappropriate investment (Paris, 28 Mar 2008).

free-public-college.rationale: As Business Secretary he kept variable tuition fees and launched the Browne review of the balance paid by taxpayers, students, graduates and employers.

free-trade.rationale: Pursued the Doha round as EU Trade Commissioner and, as ambassador, said he would negotiate tariffs down further; also cautioned that liberalisation is not 'a panacea for development'.

gm-crops.rationale: He said blanket rejection of GM ignores its role in raising food output and in adapting crops to climate change, and urged science-based approvals (Brussels, 14 Jun 2007).

limit-growth.rationale: He said climate policy must break the link between growth and emissions 'not by stifling economic growth' (Oslo, 18 Sep 2008).

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Mixed: endorsed 'markets wherever possible, government intervention wherever necessary' (2008) but in 2009 said there was too much of a mindset that markets are best left to operate freely.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Favoured 'further individualisation of our public services' with parent and patient choice; book (per reviewer) favoured competitive tendering and private-sector models.

no-bailouts.rationale: As Business Secretary he announced up to 2.3 billion pounds of state-backed loan guarantees for car makers and suppliers, while denying it was a bailout.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: In the Commons he argued for a Europe 'wider and deeper in its economic, political and defence integration' with more majority voting (11 July 1994, col. 728) and said sovereignty is pooled in the EU (4 July 2001).

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: As Northern Ireland Secretary he brought forward the order restoring the Assembly and its inclusive Executive of the pro-agreement parties (Commons, 8 May 2000, col. 501).

public-access-to-information.rationale: In the Commons he said he strongly supported the Right to Know Bill (19 Feb 1993, col. 587), which would give the public a legal right to official information.

public-ownership.rationale: As Business Secretary he pushed a part-sale of Royal Mail in 2009, against public ownership of a major industry.

reduce-immigration.rationale: He backed stronger EU border controls and returns of illegal migrants, but said Europe needs some economic migrants and warned against feeding xenophobia (Commons, 18 June 2002, col. 181).

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Book (per reviewer) would keep Conservative-era union laws including limits on secondary action.

second-chamber.rationale: He backed a democratic second chamber and attacked Opposition insincerity about it (Commons, 2 Feb 1999, col. 763; 7 Nov 2001, col. 249).

social-market-economy.rationale: Endorsed markets wherever possible with government intervention where necessary, and opposed Conservative cuts to frontline services.

state-directs-investment.rationale: As Business Secretary he launched New Industry, New Jobs with targeted support for chosen sectors, and funded a nuclear manufacturing centre and a nuclear low carbon area from the Strategic Investment Fund.

state-laws-apply-online.rationale: As Business Secretary he drove enforcement of copyright law online, including disconnecting persistent file-sharers.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Book (per reviewer) expressed scepticism towards universal benefits; evidence concerns benefits, not all social spending.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: As Trade Commissioner he resisted French calls to extend Chinese textile quotas and agreed a quota-ending deal with China.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: 1998: 'intensely relaxed about people becoming filthy rich ... as long as they pay their taxes'; The Blair Revolution (per reviewer) ruled out redistributive rates, citing need for incentives; in 2015 called Labour's mansion tax 'crude and short-termist'.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The Blair Revolution (per reviewer) backed workfare for the long-term unemployed.

notes: Appointed ambassador Dec 2024, took up post Feb 2025, dismissed by Starmer 11 Sep 2025 over Epstein links; arrested Feb 2026 on suspicion of misconduct in public office. None of this is used as evidence of ideology. Full texts of The Blair Revolution and The Third Man were not available online; book positions come from reviews and are capped at medium. Hansard and europa.eu speech archives were not reachable via search; several pages (taxresearch Guardian letter, gov.uk, BusinessGreen, Computing, committees.parliament.uk, RSA, Express and Star, Cato) returned 403/429. Pass of 2026-11-15 (rules 7): added his Commons Hansard speeches 1992-2004 (local corpus), his 2007-2008 EU Trade Commissioner speeches (EUSpeech corpus) and ministerial records from 2009; answered the candidate statements and the eight missing ones. Themes searched: economy and trade, EU and sovereignty, Lords and constitution, devolution and Northern Ireland, Iraq and the UN, immigration, climate, nuclear, biotech, higher education, broadcasting, civil liberties, intelligence services. No Hansard line shows a stated position on same-sex marriage, abortion, drugs, the death penalty, policing or prisons, so those stay null. His Iraq words (UN route first, 2002) and later praise of the invasion's results (2003) are not scored on force without UN approval. Commons votes were not searched (no division corpus). The 2006 anti-dumping duties on Chinese and Vietnamese shoes proposed by him were not opened in a readable source and are not used.
